pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mm: per-process reclaim These day, there are many platforms available in the embedded market and they are smarter than kernel which has very limited information about working set so they want to involve memory management more heavily like android's lowmemory killer and ashmem or recent many lowmemory notifier. One of the simple imagine scenario about userspace's intelligence is that platform can manage tasks as forground and background so it would be better to reclaim background's task pages for end-user's *responsibility* although it has frequent referenced pages. This patch adds new knob "reclaim under proc/<pid>/" so task manager can reclaim any target process anytime, anywhere. It could give another method to platform for using memory efficiently. It can avoid process killing for getting free memory, which was really terrible experience because I lost my best score of game I had ever after I switch the phone call while I enjoyed the game. Reclaim file-backed pages only. echo file > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim anonymous pages only. echo anon > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim all pages echo all > /proc/PID/reclaim BUG=chromium:973963 TEST=build/boot 4.4 Change-Id: I2f629f7a43289af114df27044b1d2af4a6e785bc Signed-off-by: Tim Murray <timmurray@google.com> Signed-off-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit e48b0dd9cc1fa572455434357f5678018b3458b9) modification for zone-lru list from 4.9 Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> [SR: fs/proc/base.c: add CONFIG_MMU ifdef guard for reclaim file] (cherry picked from commit 5e95f6a8aacad0289b1df3a6fbb1cfa4f99c6519 in android-msm-wahoo-4.4) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1733919 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: fix passing active page into shrink_page_list Currently, per-process reclaim calls shrink_page_list several times with zone loop. However, it's pointless that passing pages failed to reclaim in earlier trial. More severe problem is shrink_page_list can mark victim pages as PG_active so next trial of shrink_page_list with those PG_active page in the loop can warn like below. Remove the unncessary loop with zone iterator and just pass NULL as zone argument in shrink_page_list. The shrink_page_list doesn't rely on zone except writeback throttling logic in memory pressure. BACKPORT: mm: move lazily freed pages to inactive list MADV_FREE is a hint that it's okay to discard pages if there is memory pressure and we use reclaimers(ie, kswapd and direct reclaim) to free them so there is no value keeping them in the active anonymous LRU so this patch moves them to inactive LRU list's head. This means that MADV_FREE-ed pages which were living on the inactive list are reclaimed first because they are more likely to be cold rather than recently active pages. An arguable issue for the approach would be whether we should put the page to the head or tail of the inactive list. I chose head because the kernel cannot make sure it's really cold or warm for every MADV_FREE usecase but at least we know it's not *hot*, so landing of inactive head would be a comprimise for various usecases. This fixes suboptimal behavior of MADV_FREE when pages living on the active list will sit there for a long time even under memory pressure while the inactive list is reclaimed heavily. This basically breaks the whole purpose of using MADV_FREE to help the system to free memory which is might not be used. CHROMIUM: mm: perproc-reclaim: do not discarding file-backed pages With testing, I found sometime perproc-reclaim shows regression with more LMKD kill because LMKD still relies on the file-LRU size while perproc-reclaim could make the file-LRU smaller. This patch changes the policy of file-backed LRU shrinking. Instead of discarding pages of perprocess reclaim, just makes them easy-reclaimable pages, for instance, move active file pages to inactive, clear PG_referenced and pte access bits. With that, we could keep file-LRU bigger so that more change to hit in the cache while VM can shrink quickly when memory spike happens. CHROMIUM: mm: make perproc-recalim THP aware I got a report there is THP user with perproc reclaim. Thus, this patch adds THP page handling logic. It's almost same with MADV_FREE in that "let's do not split the THP page unless we are not sure because THP collapsing is never cheap". To achieve it, it splits the page only if we know there is only user for the page via page_mapcount check. lib: cros_config: Add new cros_config_probe for mosys callback Almost all platforms using cros_config have same probing logic, which can be moved into a single place. The new cros_config may simplify the boilerplate for probe function in most platforms with one single call: return cros_config_probe(intf, platform_names); It is also true that on most Unified Build platforms, the 'platform name' in cros_config model.yaml file is exactly the same as intf->name, so for mosys interfaces that are not shared by multiple overlays (Unified Build platform name is usually the overlay name), we even don't need to pass the platform names: return cros_config_probe(intf, NULL); This eliminates the need of splitting probing process into (1) match SMBIOS or firmware name in probe stage, and (2) really call cros_config_read_sku_info later or in post. platform: Move Unibuild KBL platforms to new 'poppy' folder. SKL and KBL platforms share 'glados' platform folder today. However, some of the KBL platforms have enabled cros_config and Unified Build so the implementation was pretty messy - you may see duplicated entries in both configuration (with or without cros_config). platform: Migrate Soraka, Rammus and Nautilus to new probe function For Nautilus, we have to first call cros_config_firmware_name_match to decide if it's Nautilus, try cros_config_read_sku_info; if failed, try again with forced SKU ID. However, if the cros_config_read_sku_info can fallback directly when it fail to retrieve SKU ID then we can finish probing with single step. This is more like what ARM FDT version was doing - the cros_config_read_default_sku_info_fdt. Given no platforms today really want to "force" SKU (what Nautilus needed was default SKU), we may refactor the cros_config library so now we have cros_config_read_sku_info cros_config_read_default_sku_info cros_config_probe cros_config_probe_default_sku And Nautilus can use cros_config_probe_default_sku to probe device easily. As a result, cros_config_firmware_name_match can finally be removed so we're now no longer doing firmware based matching just to decide "if this platform interface is expected to match with the cros_config installed on DUT". shill: connection: Remove Binder Connection::Binder was previously used as a way of informing dependents when a Connection goes down. However, there is currently no code in Shill that actually needs this. The only Binder client is VPNService, but this usage is unnecessary. The lifetime of a Connection is controlled by Device, which will call SetConnection(nullptr) when removing an existing Connection, so VPNService can cleanly keep track of Connection removals without the use of Connection::Binder. Functionality will be added to VirtualDevice to map virtual devices onto physical devices. Doing this in Device rather than Connection allows for VirtualDevices to map to a physical Device even when the Device is not yet up (e.g. arc_wlan0 should still map to wlan0 even when we have not yet connected to a WiFiService). This also allows us to expose Device dependency information to the D-Bus interface (e.g. if we have both a cellular dongle and l2tp VPN, there is currently no clean way to determine which PPPDevice maps to which usage from the D-Bus interface).
